memory_candidates.content: When migrating a shell script from `set -uo pipefail` to `set -euo pipefail`, a `VAR=$(cmd); status=$?` pair immediately after is an -e-hostile pattern: under -e, a failing bare assignment aborts the script on that line, before the status capture or any custom error handling can run. Fix with `if VAR=$(cmd); then status=0; else status=$?; fi` (equivalently `VAR=$(cmd) || status=$?`) -- both forms make the assignment part of a tested condition, which is -e-exempt, and preserve the captured status exactly. This pattern recurred 5 times across one script-hygiene migration (state-write.sh, task-lock.sh's retry wrapper, git-commit-scoped.sh's commit + retry, orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's verdict computation, and orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh's subprocess capture and its own findings computation) -- treat it as a near-certain finding whenever a script pairs a bare `VAR=$(cmd)` with a `status=$?`/`exit=$?` on the very next line.

A second, easy-to-miss -e-hostile bash pattern distinct from the VAR=$(cmd); status=$? anti-pattern: a bare standalone statement of the form `[ cond ] && action` (e.g. `[ -n "$x" ] && echo ... >&2`, `[ cond ] && continue`, `[ "$FLAG" = true ] && return 0`). Under `set -e` this aborts the script whenever the CONDITION is false (the common case), not just when `action` itself fails -- because a standalone `test && cmd` statement's own exit status is the test's exit status when the test is false and `cmd` never runs. This is easy to miss during an -e migration audit because it looks like ordinary short-circuit idiom and reads as harmless. Fix: append `|| true`, or restructure as an explicit `if`. Search for it with a regex like `grep -n '\[ .* \] &&[^&]*$' <file> | grep -v '||'`.

When auditing a shell script for set -e migration hazards, guard a heavily-reused leaf helper FUNCTION at its own definition (e.g. making it always `return 0` by appending `|| echo ""` to its last command) rather than guarding every individual call site. This collapsed ~15 call-site edits into 1-2 source fixes in one migration (task-lock.sh's read_holder_field and session_registry_dir). Also: `deploy-root-guard.sh`-style scripts that refuse to run outside a deployed .claude/scripts/ tree can still be live-fixture-tested without touching the real deployed tree or invoking the sanctioned-only deploy-headless.sh -- build an isolated `mktemp -d` fixture shaped like `$WORK/.claude/scripts/` (copy the script under test plus its lib/*.sh and deploy-root-guard.sh dependencies there, with `$WORK/specs/` two levels up) and exercise every subcommand/exit-code path against it.
